scope: Frozen validation of virtual-position historical-view retrieval beyond the rolling cache
settings: Existing PoseKVMemory virtual-position method, no new parameters or training

results.purpose: new seed at15.8 seconds /8-second away delay

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-~10 show the opening view: the Primemall facade with its large triangular dark roof, a centered 'Primemall' sign and a small umbrella at its base. During the RIGHT chunks (~10-40) the camera pans right past a second orange facade with garbled 'Primeect' lettering and a blue umbrella, then settles on a plaza. The plaza has an octagonal planter, two lamp posts and a zig-zag glass roof building. During the WAIT chunks (~40-120) this view is held nearly static, which is expected. During the LEFT chunks (~120-150) the camera does not retrace the outward path. It sweeps into a new glass entrance with a canopy under a doubled sign reading 'Primememall', which never appeared on the way out. It then moves through a patio of wicker chairs and large blue umbrellas and ends (~145-158) close to a Primemall-signed facade. That final view is a different viewpoint: the sign sits left of frame, large umbrellas and tables fill the foreground, and the triangular roof is only cropped at the top. The opening composition (centered sign, distant small umbrella, full roof silhouette) is not recovered. The apparent forward translation toward the building and the new entrance geometry are not explained by pure yaw.
A.failure_classification: Forgetting / hallucinated return geometry. The leftward return synthesizes unseen structures (a new entrance, a patio and a duplicated sign text) instead of re-rendering the outward path. It also drifts in position, arriving at a similar-looking but different viewpoint of the same-branded building. Some camera-control drift (implied translation) is also present.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-~120 are essentially identical to A: the same opening facade, the same rightward pan, and the same held plaza view during WAIT. During the LEFT chunks (~120-150) the camera retraces the outward path in reverse order. First the planter and plaza, then the orange facade with the same garbled 'Primeect'/'Prmmgnl' lettering and the blue umbrella with seated figure. Then the triangular-roof Primemall building re-enters from the left, and the frame settles on it (~145-158). The landmark identity is preserved: same roof silhouette, a readable 'Primemall' sign, the orange diamond cladding and the right-side wing. However, the final framing is offset. The building sits in the right half of the frame rather than centered, and the view is somewhat closer. A new blue pylon sign and a storefront with 'NEHGEP'-like lettering appear at left that were not in the opening frame, and foreground umbrellas are larger. Transitions are smooth, with no hard cuts.
B.failure_classification: Minor camera-control/pose drift (yaw overshoot or positional offset on return) plus small hallucinated peripheral content (pylon sign, left storefront). The core landmark and the ordering of the intermediate scenery are remembered consistently, so this is largely not a forgetting failure.

visual_assessment.reasoning: Both videos share an identical outward turn and hold, so the comparison hinges on the LEFT return. B retraces the outward scenery in correct reverse order and ends on the same Primemall building with its distinctive roof and sign intact. Its imperfections are an offset final framing and some new peripheral signage. A instead invents an unseen entrance and patio with garbled duplicated sign text ('Primememall'), and it reaches a Primemall facade from a clearly different, closer viewpoint. A's similar final building should not be credited as a recovery, since it was reached through hallucinated geometry rather than a consistent return. B is not a perfect return to the exact starting view, hence medium confidence.

results.purpose: next unused held-out image in frozen split; fountain scene

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 show the start view: a tiered stone fountain in the center, a wooden barrel to its left, small benches at the left and right edges, a reddish-leaf tree behind, and a building and bamboo-like trees in the background. During the RIGHT chunks (about frames 10-40) the camera pans right continuously. It passes a white bench, cypresses, snowy mountains and a planter barrel. It then passes a backlit dark fountain with a lattice bench and reaches a view of a broad-leaf tree, a barrel, red flowers and a hedge. That view holds steady through the WAIT period (about frames 40-119), with only minor shimmer. During the LEFT chunks (about frames 120-150) the pan reverses through the same intermediate landmarks in reverse order: dark fountain, then cypresses and mountains with the planter barrel, then the white bench. At about frames 140-144 the original tiered fountain returns with the same barrel on its left, white bench on its right, reddish tree behind and background structure. The rotation then continues past the start heading. The final WAIT frames (about 150-158) show a bench in tree shade with the start fountain's rim at the right edge, and the same white bench and barrel in the background.
A.failure_classification: Minor camera-control error: the left turn overshoots, so the final resting heading is offset to the left of the start view rather than matching it exactly. The return pan is also not symmetric in pacing with the outbound pan. No memory failure: the landmarks seen on the way back keep their identity and layout. No sign text is present to check.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-119 are essentially identical to A: the same start fountain scene, the same rightward pan to the tree/barrel/red-flower view, and the same stable WAIT period. During the LEFT chunks the camera does pan left: the dark backlit fountain reappears around frames 120-125. After that the scene does not retrace the outbound path. Instead of cypresses with the planter barrel, white bench and the start fountain, new content appears: bare deciduous trees, a long hedge with several lattice-back benches (including a double bench), a broad mountain ridge, and a fountain lit from the front with fleur-de-lis ornamentation and a bright blue pool. The final frames (about 150-158) show this ornate fountain centered among lattice benches, cypresses and a hedge. None of the start-view landmarks are visible: no barrel left of the fountain, no reddish tree, no building or bamboo trees, no lawn layout matching the start. The fountain's form and lighting change from the dark silhouette to the new ornate design during the pan.
B.failure_classification: Spatial forgetting / hallucination on return. Camera control works (a leftward yaw is visibly executed), but the revisited region is re-synthesized as a different place. The fountain's identity morphs implausibly mid-pan, and the final view is a new scene rather than the starting viewpoint.

visual_assessment.reasoning: Both videos share an identical outbound turn and WAIT segment, so the difference lies entirely in the return. A retraces the outbound landmarks in reverse order and clearly re-presents the original fountain, barrel, white bench and background. Its only flaw is a heading overshoot at the end, which is a camera-control imprecision, not forgetting. B rotates as commanded but invents new geometry on the way back (multiple lattice benches, bare trees, a differently ornamented fountain) and ends in a scene inconsistent with the start. That is a memory/consistency failure with an implausible identity transition. A's return comes from continuous motion, not a reset, so recognizing it is warranted.

caveat: Fixed-path memory mechanism validation, not an adaptive PlayWorld score or a claim about minute-long worlds.
